findings.title: ExplanationPart's OffsetsViaWearer gate drops the entad line from the gear's own equipped-offset report
findings.detail: ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats builds the info-card row for each of the def's equippedStatOffsets. It sets 'Final value' from StatWorker.StatOffsetFromGear(req.Thing, stat), which includes Patch_StatOffsetFromGear's entad offset, and then lists stat.parts[i].ExplanationPart(req) with req = the gear. With OffsetsViaWearer true for gear, StatPart_Entad.ExplanationPart (StatPart_Entad.cs:65) emits no offset line, so the card shows Base +X and Final +X+e with nothing explaining e. The helper is right in TransformValue, where the number is made (the postfix adds the offset, so the part must not add it too). It is wrong in ExplanationPart, because there the number already includes the offset. One change: remove `!offsetsViaWearer &&` from the statOffsets loop at StatPart_Entad.cs:65, keep the `known` gate, and leave TransformValue as it is.

findings.title: The same equipped-offset row shows hidden entad offsets in its Final value
findings.detail: Patch_StatOffsetFromGear adds the full WearerOffset, hidden part included (EntadWearerStats.cs:157-160). Patch_InfoTextLineFromGear subtracts hiddenPart for the pawn's gear lines, but nothing does that for the gear's own ThingDef equipped-offset row, so an unrevealed trait shows up as an unexplained change in that row's Final value. This was already the case before this change; it is worth knowing when the explanation line above is restored, because only revealed offsets will be listed.

findings.title: OffsetsViaWearer gates offsets only; wearer-stat factors still multiply inside StatOffsetFromGear
findings.detail: StatPart_Entad.cs:25-26 applies statFactors without the helper. When vanilla runs parts over gear inside StatOffsetFromGear, an entad factor on a wearer stat multiplies the def's equippedStatOffset before the postfix adds the entad offset. IsCompatible only allows wearer factors on defs that list the stat in statBases (EntadTraitDef.cs:448), so this is rare. If it is intended, a word in the helper's comment would make that clear. This is my reading of the call order; I did not observe it in a run.
